clue.text: "There is no trusting —" Sheridan (The School for Scandal)

definitions.text: "There is no trusting —" Sheridan (The School for Scandal)

parts.words: "There is no trusting —" Sheridan (The School for Scandal)
parts.note: a quotation to complete: the missing word is what Sheridan's line says cannot be trusted, namely how things look on the outside

explanation.surface: A line from Sheridan's comedy The School for Scandal with its last word left blank.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a fill-in-the-blank quotation rather than wordplay: the full line from The School for Scandal ends with the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The line warns that outward looks and impressions are deceptive, which is the word that completes it.

clue.text: Lady's maid having trouble after a great start

indicators.note: after places the trouble piece behind the opening pieces

parts.note: great means big
to ail is to trouble, as an illness does

explanation.surface: A lady's maid who has problems after a promising beginning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start' just tells you A BIG comes first, with AIL following it.
explanation.definitionFit: Abigail was once a common name for a waiting-woman, after a character in a 17th-century play.

clue.text: Selects simple tools

definitions.meaning: pointed implements for breaking ground or ice

explanation.surface: Someone choosing a few basic tools.
explanation.definitionFit: To choose is to make picks, and pointed digging implements are also called that.

clue.text: Bluster and rage on car breaking down

indicators.note: a car breaking down suggests the words are smashed up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone blustering and raging when their car breaks down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking down' shuffles RAGE, ON and CAR together.
explanation.definitionFit: Bluster is loud, swaggering self-importance, a show of haughty conceit.

clue.text: A medical man's book

parts.note: a medical man is an MO (medical officer); the 's adds an S

explanation.surface: A book belonging to a doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: Here the 's is read literally as an extra S after MO.
explanation.definitionFit: Amos is one of the minor prophets, a book of the Old Testament.

clue.text: Shy with press but not yielding

parts.note: to shy is to throw, or cast
to press clothes is to iron them

explanation.surface: Someone shy with reporters yet stubbornly refusing to give way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'press' looks like the newspapers; it is the verb for flattening laundry.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hard and rigid, like a guarantee or an alibi, is described as firm and unbending in this way.

clue.text: Portly porter

definitions.meaning: a dark beer, of which a stronger kind bears this name

explanation.surface: A fat railway porter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'porter' is a dark beer here, not a luggage carrier.
explanation.definitionFit: A plump person is called stout, and stout is a strong dark beer like porter.

clue.text: A player gets about and maybe stares around

indicators.note: around has the shuffled letters sit round the single letter
maybe says the word stares is only one possible order of its letters

parts.note: C stands for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A performer gets about and perhaps stares at the audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' rearranges STARES into ATRESS, which goes 'around' C: A-C-TRESS.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who plays roles on stage or screen is a performer.

clue.text: Regulation colours

definitions.meaning: a set norm or official specification
a flag, as in a regiment's colours

explanation.surface: Rules about uniform colours.
explanation.definitionFit: A norm laid down is a benchmark, and a regimental flag is also called by this name.

clue.text: Contract debts without any interest

parts.note: to contract a debt is to incur it
IOUs are written promises to repay debts

explanation.surface: Taking on debts without paying any interest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interest' sounds financial but means curiosity.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who lacks curiosity is indifferent and unquestioning.

clue.text: Eight have to turn and the rest back in

indicators.note: this word is a container marker: it says one piece is placed inside the other, and the clue words of the pieces show which way round
turn tells us the little word to flips its two letters
back says the abbreviation for the rest is written right to left

parts.note: etc., short for et cetera, means and the rest

explanation.surface: Eight people have to turn round while the others go back inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' makes OT; ETC read 'back' gives CTE, which goes 'in' it: O-CTE-T.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of eight musicians or lines of verse forms this set.

clue.text: Give out a dope and gin mixture

parts.note: a dope is a fool, an ass

indicators.note: a mixture of gin suggests its letters stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A fool handing out a gin cocktail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixture' rearranges GIN into IGN after ASS.
explanation.definitionFit: To allot or allocate a task is to hand it out.

clue.text: Step outside first, showing restraint

indicators.note: outside means the dance word goes around the ordinal

parts.note: a step is a dance
1st, written as letters, is IST

explanation.surface: Someone stepping outside first to show self-control.
explanation.walkthrough: IST is the crossword way of writing 1st.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping one's distance is reserve or aloofness, holding oneself back.

clue.text: Dropping the wrong entry in the record-book

indicators.note: an entry in a book is something put inside it, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: a log is a book of records, as on a ship
a wrong is a sin

explanation.surface: Removing an incorrect entry from the record book.
explanation.definitionFit: Losing something is letting it go or mislaying it, as with dropped catches or points.

clue.text: An American writer having some say over delay

indicators.note: over in a down clue puts the first piece above the second
some means only part of the word say is used

parts.note: to linger is to delay

explanation.surface: An American author with some influence over a hold-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' takes SA from 'say'; 'over' puts it above LINGER in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: J. D. Salinger wrote The Catcher in the Rye.

clue.text: Stays in favour of omnivorous animals

parts.note: to be for something is to favour it
bears eat both plants and meat

explanation.surface: Remains in support of animals that eat anything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stays' looks like remains; it means holds back, refrains.
explanation.definitionFit: To refrain or hold back from acting is to restrain oneself.

clue.text: Game that's of little consequence

definitions.meaning: a board game in which balls are struck into scoring holes

explanation.surface: A game that hardly matters.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both a pinball-like table game and a word for a trifle or trivial matter.

clue.text: Agonised characters going to town in the USA

indicators.note: the letters of the word set off in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Tormented people heading for an American town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters going' rearranges the eight letters of AGONISED.
explanation.definitionFit: A Californian city near the Mexican border.

clue.text: Autumn holds a Communist back just a trifle

indicators.note: holds means the season word grips the other letters

parts.note: fall is the American word for autumn

indicators.note: back says the pair a plus the Communist is read in reverse

parts.note: a Red is a Communist

explanation.surface: In autumn a Communist is held back a little.
explanation.walkthrough: A RED read 'back' gives DERA, which FALL 'holds': FAL-DERA-L.
explanation.definitionFit: Falderal means nonsense or a showy but worthless thing, a mere bauble.

clue.text: Make-up expert's work

parts.note: reads like a cosmetic artist's job, but means the output of someone expert at making things up, a novelist

explanation.surface: The work of a cosmetics artist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make-up' is stories made up, not cosmetics.
explanation.definitionFit: Novels and invented stories are the product of someone who makes things up.

clue.text: A midnight raid disorganised a Moroccan place

parts.note: the middle letter of night

indicators.note: a disorganised raid has its letters thrown out of order

explanation.surface: A midnight attack goes badly wrong in Morocco.
explanation.walkthrough: 'midnight' is read as mid-night, the centre letter G; 'disorganised' turns RAID into ADIR.
explanation.definitionFit: Agadir is a port city on Morocco's Atlantic coast.

clue.text: Book for husband

definitions.meaning: to book is to secure in advance
to husband resources is to conserve them

explanation.surface: Reserving something for one's spouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'husband' is the verb, to use sparingly.
explanation.definitionFit: To book a seat is to keep it in advance, and to husband supplies is to save them up.

clue.text: Claims read by ministers

parts.note: to con is an old word for to study or read
to minister to someone is to tend them

explanation.surface: Claims read out by government ministers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ministers' is a verb, to look after.
explanation.definitionFit: To assert or maintain a position is to argue for it.

clue.text: Take in about a hundred and fifty to gain acclaim

indicators.note: about means the eating word wraps round the numerals

parts.note: to take in food is to eat
C is the Roman numeral for 100
L is the Roman numeral for 50

explanation.surface: Accepting around 150 to win praise.
explanation.definitionFit: Eclat is brilliant success or applause, conspicuous acclaim.

clue.text: Crooks find it over-quiet in an ocean-going vessel

indicators.note: in places the excess-and-soft letters within the ship letters

parts.note: SS is a steamship
too means overly, excessively
p is piano, quiet in music

explanation.surface: Criminals discover it is too quiet aboard a liner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crooks' is a verb, bends forward.
explanation.definitionFit: To crook the back is to bend or hunch it.

clue.text: Exceed some set limit-flout Government ruling

indicators.note: some means only part of the words is used, the letters running across them

explanation.surface: Going beyond a set limit, defying government rules.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across 'flout Government'.
explanation.definitionFit: To outgo is to surpass or go beyond.

clue.text: Blackleg giving direction to hired transport

parts.note: S is south, a compass direction
a cab is a taxi, hired transport

explanation.surface: A strike-breaker giving instructions to a taxi.
explanation.walkthrough: Blackleg is British for a worker who breaks a strike.
explanation.definitionFit: A scab is a strike-breaker who keeps working.

clue.text: The best one to distribute

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
to deal cards is to distribute them

explanation.surface: The best person to share things out.
explanation.definitionFit: Perfect, the most desirable model.

clue.text: Steps taken to move effortlessly

parts.note: steps you stand on while they carry you up or down without walking

explanation.surface: Measures adopted to make things easy.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving stairways in shops and stations carry people between floors.

clue.text: Worrying more, but lose anyway

indicators.note: anyway means in any order at all

explanation.surface: Fretting more, yet losing regardless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'anyway' shuffles MORE, BUT and LOSE together.
explanation.definitionFit: Something causing concern and bother is vexing.
